summary: Complete independent negative audit of the exact sealed Shiji 064 input: all 51 owned Chinese units, 39 date/hint items and 15 people reviewed. Verified primary cross-chapter chronology and pinned the modern BC table alignment separately from ancient text. Findings include posthumous reception presented as living activity, ancestral/clan event-owner substitutions, a He/Wei textual conflation, overbroad recommendation dates, omitted relative/absolute death context, and unsupported grievance/composition endpoints. Documented historical uncertainty without declaring disputed people legendary. No repairs, canonical edits, queue operations, publication or paid inference were performed; this report is not approval.

itemChecks.event: p001 Rangju's recommendation and appointment by Lord Jing, not later reception of his methods.
itemChecks.reason: The subject owns this appointment. BC 548 is Jing's accession year (Shiji 014 s4723/s4727), not his first numbered year, BC 547 (s4739/s4743). BC 490 is Jing's death (s5651/s5655), a defensible outer reign bound but not the best endpoint for this episode: the recommending Yan Ying dies in Jing 48, BC 500 (032 s0442/s0447; 014 s5491/s5495). Carry that tighter recommendation constraint into the appointment's contextual dating rather than suggesting it could occur in 499-490. These are conventional historical year labels, not converted Gregorian days. The independent historicity hold on p001 remains.

景公召穰苴，與語兵事，大說之，以為將軍，將兵捍燕晉之師。

Preserve this sequence and its source-qualified uncertainty instead of using an unexplained full-reign interval. Do not infer a Gregorian appointment date.
